statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is low while broad market Stress remains extreme.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON because Tail is below 20%; Stress remains extreme around the U.S. event cluster and geopolitical risk.
headline: Low Tail, extreme Stress ahead of the U.S. event cluster
body: Fresh reporting shows modestly firmer U.S. futures and easing bond yields, while the latest directly time-stamped delayed NQ quote is near flat. No current evidence verifies persistent no-retracement NQ structure. Oil remains near $95 Brent amid U.S.-Iran/Hormuz risk, with major U.S. releases beginning at 12:30 UTC.

lookbackSummary: Published history shows elevated Tail during parts of the prior U.S. session, then low-Tail mixed structure overnight. The 22:00 UTC slot has no published assessment and remains unavailable.
outlookSummary: Tail stays below the blocking threshold in the base forecast, peaking at 24% around the U.S. release and cash-open window. Any higher Tail state remains conditional on observed persistent NQ extension and poor retracement quality.

forecast.analysis: Current evidence is mixed: delayed NQ is near flat and broad U.S. futures are modestly firmer. No fresh evidence verifies persistent no-retracement NQ structure.
drivers: Delayed NQ is near flat, not persistently one-way

forecast.analysis: Risk sensitivity rises as U.S. releases approach. Tail remains low unless NQ starts holding near an extreme with shallow or failed retracements.
Pre-release liquidity can increase whipsaw risk. Tail rises modestly, but a blocking state still requires observed one-way structure rather than event proximity.
drivers: Observed path persistence is still required

forecast.analysis: The 12:30 UTC trade, claims, productivity and Waller cluster creates the main danger window. WATCH is conditional on post-release path quality, not the event itself.
drivers: 12:30 UTC trade, claims, productivity and Waller cluster

forecast.analysis: Post-data trading and the U.S. cash open overlap. WATCH persists if price discovery is disorderly; persistent extension with weak pullbacks would be the key escalation signal.
drivers: U.S. cash-open auction follows the data cluster

forecast.analysis: ISM Services at 14:00 UTC extends the event window. Tail stays at WATCH unless the observed response develops repeated extension and failed mean reversion.
drivers: Failed retracements would be the escalation signal

forecast.analysis: After ISM, Tail should ease if retracements return and cross-assets stabilize. Continued one-way NQ action would invalidate that normalization.
With the main data cluster past, the base path shifts toward mixed trade. Tail remains WATCH only while residual post-event continuation risk is unresolved.
Tail returns low if the session remains two-sided. Holding near a session extreme with repeated failed pullbacks would be the main contrary signal.
drivers: Session-extreme holding is the main warning

forecast.analysis: Mid-session risk is lower under an orderly path. Headline volatility can keep Stress high without proving persistent mean-reversion failure.
drivers: Headline volatility alone does not prove Tail

forecast.analysis: Fed remarks at 19:00 UTC are a later headline checkpoint. Tail remains low unless rates and NQ align into sustained directional continuation.
drivers: Rates sensitivity is a late-session checkpoint

forecast.analysis: After that checkpoint, event intensity should fade. A fresh geopolitical or oil shock would raise Stress first and Tail only if NQ becomes persistently directional.
drivers: Oil and geopolitical risk remain latent

forecast.analysis: Late-session continuation versus reversal becomes the main path test. Tail remains low unless NQ holds near an extreme with poor retracement quality.
Into the close, available retracements keep Tail low. A sharp closing drive aligned with yields or oil would challenge the mixed baseline.
drivers: Aligned yields or oil could amplify a closing drive

forecast.analysis: Early post-close conditions should carry lower Tail. Corporate headlines may lift Stress, but only persistent futures repricing would materially raise Tail.
Early Asia trade is expected to remain low-Tail if futures stay two-sided. The next day's employment report is a future checkpoint, not current Tail evidence.
drivers: Employment report remains a future checkpoint

forecast.analysis: Asia-session Tail stays low unless a geopolitical discontinuity or sustained futures trend appears. Ordinary volatility without path persistence mainly affects Stress.
drivers: Geopolitical discontinuity is the main overnight risk

forecast.analysis: Tail remains low if overnight pullbacks continue to function. Stress edges higher as the employment report moves closer, without assuming any release outcome.
As Europe approaches, pre-event positioning can lift Stress. Tail rises only if overnight price action becomes persistently directional with weak retracements.
The European handoff may increase positioning activity. Holding near an overnight extreme with repeated failed pullbacks would be the key Tail warning.
drivers: Overnight-extreme holding would be a Tail warning

forecast.analysis: Pre-employment-report positioning becomes more relevant. Tail stays below WATCH unless a clean directional trend develops before Europe.
drivers: Pre-event positioning can raise whipsaw risk

forecast.analysis: Stress rises as the employment report approaches. Tail remains low unless persistent overnight structure and cross-asset alignment are already evident.
drivers: Employment report is closer but unobserved
Cross-asset alignment would be needed for higher Tail

forecast.analysis: The final forecast hour stays low-Tail but high-Stress ahead of the later 12:30 UTC employment report. Any higher state remains path-dependent.
drivers: 12:30 UTC Employment Situation is later in the day

forecastDetail.comment: Current evidence is mixed with no verified persistent NQ mean-reversion failure; event and geopolitical Stress remains extreme.
Low Tail persists if the Europe-to-U.S. handoff stays orderly; renewed oil or rate pressure would mainly lift Stress.
Approaching releases lift sensitivity, but higher Tail still requires observed directional persistence and weak retracements.
Pre-release liquidity can raise whipsaw risk; Tail stays below WATCH unless one-way structure begins to emerge.
WATCH reflects the 12:30 UTC danger window conditionally; a block requires post-release persistence and poor retracement quality.
Post-data and cash-open structure is decisive; persistent extension sustains WATCH while two-sided trade would normalize Tail.
